mechanism: Erythromycin may inhibit CYP3A4 metabolism and cause electrolyte disturbances; chlorthalidone causes hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia which increase risk of QT prolongation with macrolide antibiotics.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes (particularly potassium and magnesium) and ECG during concurrent use; consider alternative antibiotic if possible; correct electrolyte deficiencies before starting erythromycin.
